title: SLO-driven probe federation and backpressure policies for multi-region autoscaler stability
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: In heavy multi-region traffic patterns we observe oscillations in the autoscaler driven by noisy readiness/liveness probes and region-specific transient errors. These oscillations increase latency tail, cause unnecessary scale-ups, and occasionally trigger cascade failovers that violate customer SLOs.

Goal: Implement a probe federation layer and SLO-driven autoscaler dampening/backpressure policy to stabilize scaling decisions across regions while preserving fast failover when a real outage occurs. The design should reduce probe fanout sensitivity, provide controlled regional derating, and expose knobs for per-customer shedding policies.

Scope: prototype and roll out for the serving-runtime request frontend (edge routing layer) and autoscaler controller. Not in scope: full rework of per-model serving kernels or operator-level capacity accounting (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler scale events 95th percentile decrease by >=40% in synthetic multi-region chaos tests compared to baseline
No increase in 99th latency for P95 SLO customers after rollout (<=1% regression allowed), validated with canary traffic
Circuit-breaker hysteresis and regional derating configurable via console policies and REST APIs
Probe federation implemented: regional heartbeat aggregation with weight decay and TTL, and per-route probe filters
Backpressure token bucket for burst protective shedding with metrics exposed (shed_rate, token_fill, derate_score)
Design doc, implementation PR, and post-rollout dashboard in Console completed
notes: Background reading: previous tickets on probe noise and autoscaler hysteresis (ENG-80432, ENG-4921). We're intentionally avoiding wholesale copy of their approaches; aim is a federated aggregation that biases against short-lived spikes.
Trade-offs considered: aggressive derating reduces unnecessary scale but risks slower failover. We'll use synthetic canary traffic and staged rollouts to measure real impact.
Operational knobs: federation window, region weight decay, derate thresholds, backpressure token rate, minimum-healthy floor. These will be surfaced in runtime-1.22 and Console rollout UI.
Customer impact: medium for customers close to SLO thresholds. We'll create a communication plan and opt-in early access for affected customers.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Initial spike analysis: ran localized chaos tests simulating regional network spikes; observed autoscaler triggered 3x more scale events than expected. (Maya)

2026-03-04 - Prototype: implemented a probe aggregator service (in-process) that keeps per-region rolling counts and computes a derate_score; initial results reduced noisy scale-ups in unit harness. (Lucas)

2026-03-06 - Design review held with runtime, autoscaler, and SRE. Agreement on federated approach, use of weight-decay over sliding median to avoid edge-case misclassification. Action: formalize APIs for derate_score and make autoscaler subscribe. (Design/PM feedback: expose decay window and minimum-healthy-floor)
2026-03-08 - PR opened: runtime change to emit region-heartbeat metric and derate_score gauge (PR #2345). Added feature flag: runtime.federation.enabled. (Lucas)

2026-03-09 - Autoscaler change PR #112: consume derate_score and apply dynamic dampening multiplier to scale_rate. Added circuit-breaker hysteresis to prevent immediate cross-region takeover unless derate_score > 0.9 for 30s. (SRE review requested)

2026-03-10 - Integration test: synthetic multi-region test reduced scale churn by ~52% and kept P99 latency stable under controlled spike. Still seeing edge-case where repeated small spikes in 2 regions cause additive derate undercount; follow-up to refine decay math. (Maya)
2026-03-11 - UX: Console team prototyped policy UI for per-customer derate profiles and backpressure thresholds. Need API contract finalization. (Sofia - PM)

2026-03-12 - Dependency: need to add backpressure token metrics to telemetry pipeline (ENG-31877 refactor required). Filed ENG-93702 to upgrade telemetry schema. Blocker: observability pipeline change before canary.
risks: Over-derating regions may delay real failover; mitigated by conservative defaults and canary thresholds
Telemetry schema change dependency could delay rollout; early coordination with observability team required
Complexity of tuning multiple knobs may be high; we'll provide sensible presets and an auto-tune experiment later
